steps.title: Feedback
steps.body: Information received by a performer about the outcome of their action or the quality of their performance. Feedback is essential for learning and improvement as it completes the information processing loop.

steps.title: Positive Feedback
steps.body: Feedback that focuses on what the performer did correctly. It reinforces good technique and encourages the performer to repeat successful actions.

steps.title: Negative Feedback
steps.body: Feedback that identifies what the performer did incorrectly. It highlights errors and suggests corrections to improve future performance. It is NOT criticism - it is constructive information about what went wrong.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: "Negative feedback" does NOT mean telling someone they are bad. It means identifying what went wrong and providing constructive correction. If a coach just says "that was terrible" without explaining how to improve, this is criticism, not negative feedback.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know all six types of feedback: positive, negative, KR, KP, extrinsic, intrinsic Always use sporting examples to illustrate each type Remember: negative feedback ≠ criticism. Negative feedback is constructive and corrective KR = outcome/result; KP = technique/process - this is a very common exam distinction Link feedback type to the stage of learning (beginner vs elite) Feedback types can overlap - e.g. a comment can be both extrinsic AND negative AND KP
